beats.text: Plan the chain before calculating. Part a: E equals V times I times t, then the calibration factor, then a comparison with the water alone. Part b: moles of each solution from concentration times volume, then the limiting reactant. Part c: the corrected temperature rise from the graph. Part d: the heat from the calibration factor and the corrected rise, divided by the limiting amount, with a sign.
Parts a, b and c all feed part d, so an error in any of them carries through to the enthalpy. Parts e and f are reasoning parts: they test whether you understand what the numbers mean.
